title: France on edge: from school protests to a test for Macron

scenes.title: France on edge: how school protests became a test for Macron
scenes.say: It started at school gates. Now it's a national test for Emmanuel Macron.

scenes.title: From classrooms to the streets
scenes.say: In mid-September, students blocked schools over teacher shortages and admissions. On 17 October, protests turned violent and over 2,000 people were detained.
scenes.speak: In mid-September, students blocked schools over teacher shortages and admissions. On the seventeenth of October, protests turned violent and over two thousand people were detained.

scenes.label: police and gendarmes deployed, about 20% more than the week before
scenes.say: So on 24 October, France deployed 70,000 police and gendarmes, about a fifth more than the weekend before.
scenes.speak: So on the twenty-fourth of October, France deployed seventy thousand police and gendarmes, about a fifth more than the weekend before.

scenes.title: How many marched on 24 October?
scenes.say: The government counted 410,000 marchers. Organisers claimed nearly 800,000.
scenes.speak: The government counted four hundred and ten thousand marchers. Organisers claimed nearly eight hundred thousand.

scenes.title: Clashes in cities across France
scenes.source: Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez; Euronews; AP
scenes.say: Police fired tear gas in Paris, Marseille, Lyon, Bordeaux, Lille and beyond. Nearly 1,000 people were arrested.
scenes.speak: Police fired tear gas in Paris, Marseille, Lyon, Bordeaux, Lille and beyond. Nearly a thousand people were arrested.

scenes.title: The pressure isn't easing
scenes.say: Macron has promised more teachers and an overhaul of university admissions. But the yellow vests plan new rallies on 31 October, with an election due in 2027.
scenes.speak: Macron has promised more teachers and an overhaul of university admissions. But the yellow vests plan new rallies on the thirty-first of October, with an election due in twenty twenty-seven.

scenes.text: A state can reinforce streets. It cannot resolve dissatisfaction over education, affordability and inequality through policing alone.
scenes.say: Policing can hold the streets. It can't fix schools, prices or inequality.
